extracted.intended_audience: Clinicians, medical educators, and early-career academics serving as peer reviewers for medical/academic journals (particularly medical education journals).
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for performing and improving peer review of manuscripts submitted to medical journals, covering ethical considerations, how to read and assess manuscripts, how to write organized reviews, and long-term reviewer development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer to be a reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer to be a reviewer for a journal that you read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually requires an e-mail to the editorial office with a brief summary of your background and interests. Serving as a reviewer is vital to advancing the field and is a way to learn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actively address ethical issues/conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: When a review invitation arrives, determine if you have a conflict of interest or a competing interest (1 or more authors are a friend, family member, or current collaborator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a conflict of interest, decline the review. If unsure whether a conflict exists, contact the journal editor for advice. Also, do not disclose any information from the manuscript to anyone without the editor's permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have insufficient expertise in the topic area, decline the review. If you cannot submit the report within the requested time frame, ask for an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you accept the review, do not disclose manuscript information. Maintain courteous and supportive tone in communications and in the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the journal, its audience, and publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each journal has a unique audience, focus, manuscript categories, and criteria (word limit, number of tables and figures, section headings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review past issues and the journal's guidelines to ensure the manuscript fits the journal's audience and format before assessing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess topical relevance and interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper address a topic of current interest and relevance to the journal's audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the subject matter will engage the readership and aligns with the journal's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess originality or value in corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Present new information or corroborate information that is not well accepted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript advances knowledge or meaningfully verifies contested findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess use of and citation of relevant literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite and discuss relevant literature to justify the need for the study?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether prior work is adequately referenced and whether the study rationale is grounded in existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess clarity of research purpose or question
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear research purpose or question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-defined purpose/question should guide the methods and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess methods for sufficient detail and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods in sufficient detail so that others could replicate the study?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clear descriptions of participants, procedures, measures, data collection, and analysis sufficient for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess appropriateness of analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the results with accepted quantitative or qualitative methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the statistical or qualitative analytic methods are appropriate, correctly applied, and adequately reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess clarity and usability of results presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the results in easy to read (text) or view (tables, figures) formats?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that tables/figures are clear, labeled, and that text describes key findings without redundancy or omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess discussion and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the results in light of what is already known, along with the methodological limitations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors interpret findings in context, acknowledge limitations, and avoid overstating implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess appropriateness of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide conservative conclusions from the study findings, without editorializing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should follow from the data and analyses and avoid speculation beyond the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess fit within journal format and category
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit within the journal's format and category restrictions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the manuscript conforms to word limits, section structure, and the type/category of article the journal publishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess clarity of narrative and flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story in a clear manner with good flow?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate overall readability, organization, logical progression of ideas, and whether the manuscript communicates its message effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper through and organize your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the paper through and organize your review, considering relevance, originality, literature, and format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Assessing Key Elements' as a checklist when reading; form an overall impression before writing detailed comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize your written review (tone, summary, numbered comments, labeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a courteous, supportive tone, provide a 1- to 2-sentence overall summary of the paper's purpose. Then, section by section, provide numbered comments to which the author(s) should respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label comments with section, page number, or line number(s) to direct authors. Focus on content, clarity, and organization rather than grammar, punctuation, or spelling. For papers needing an overall rewrite for correct English use, flag the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide recommendation to editors (accept/revise/reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide your recommendation to editors regarding accept, revise, reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide a decision to authors (editors make the final disposition given pipeline context). Provide confidential comments to editors when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting an invitation: consider conflicts, expertise match, and time
rubrics_metrics.description: Before accepting an invitation to review, consider potential conflicts, the match between your expertise and the paper, and your time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline if you lack expertise or cannot complete within a reasonable timeframe; request extensions when appropriate; consult the editor when in doubt about conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use structured reviewer report formats and seek feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to enhance peer-review skills by using a structured reviewer report format, seeking feedback, and mentoring others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured formats and checklists can improve consistency; ask editors for feedback on your reviews and compare with other reviewers when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term reviewer development and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve reviews by seeking editors' feedback, reading your own manuscripts as if you were a reviewer, seeking advice from senior colleagues, mentoring junior colleagues, and forming or joining reviewer groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider joining a team-based coaching approach, journal clubs for reviewers, or becoming a member of a journal editorial board after honing reviewing skills.
